# Complete the customer billing-schedule migration

Finish the service-to-customer migration for recurring billing. Creating a customer must create a monthly billing schedule only when that customer has an offering. When an existing customer gains or changes an `offeringId`, replace any previous billing schedule with a customer-level schedule; an already-missing old schedule is not an error. Preserve the authenticated subject and business ID in the scheduler configuration.

Billing jobs receive `businessID` on the scheduler record and `customerId` in `scheduleParameters`. Resolve the customer and its offering, derive the offering billing-cycle time range, call the existing usage-total invoice path with that exact customer and range, and persist a billing record containing the returned invoice ID. Report processing failures through the existing audit channel instead of leaving the queue job with a partially stored billing record.

Route billing scheduler emissions to `scheduler_billing_queue` with the `billingReport` consumer name. All non-billing measurements must continue to use the normal scheduler queue and their dimension consumer. Finally, a usage read for a customer without an offering should return an empty result rather than fail.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the current state of the migration.

steps.message:
The migration is complete. `npm run build` and `npm run test:ci -- --runInBand` both pass (43 suites / 70 tests).

What changed:

**Customer-level billing schedules** (`src/customer/customer.service.ts`)
- `create` now only registers the monthly billing schedule when the customer actually has an `offeringId`; otherwise it logs and skips.
- New private helpers `createBillingSchedule` / `removeBillingSchedule` centralize the scheduler calls (`schedulerID = customerId`, `schedulerType.billing`, monthly rate, `scheduleParameters: { customerId, businessID }`, plus the authenticated `subject` and `businessID`). `remove` reuses the tolerant helper.
- `update({...}, subject?)` replaces the schedule when the customer gains or changes an `offeringId`: it removes any pre-existing schedule (a `NotFoundException` is swallowed — a missing old schedule is not an error) and creates the customer-level one. `customer.controller.ts:update` now forwards the authenticated `sub`.

**Billing job processing** (`src/billing/billing.service.ts`, `billing.module.ts`)
- The processor reads `businessID` off the scheduler record and `customerId` from `scheduleParameters`, resolves the customer plus its offering (falling back to `OfferingService` when only an `offeringId` is present), derives the range via `Billing.billingCycleToTimeRange(offering.billingCycle)`, calls `invoicesService.generateInvoiceForUsageTotal({ businessID, customerId, start, end })`, and persists a `Billing` point with the returned `invoiceId`.
- Whole run is wrapped so failures publish `AuditService.publishEvent(... AuditScope.ERROR)` instead of leaving a partially written billing record; customers without an offering are logged and skipped. Dependencies are optional-injected (with `InvoicesService`/`ServicesService` fallbacks for the customer service) so the processor still instantiates in the existing module wiring; `BillingModule` now imports the customer module.

**Scheduler routing** (`src/scheduler/scheduler.service.ts:227`)
- `emitOne` sends billing emissions to `scheduler_billing_queue` under `billingScheduleConsumers.billingReport`; every other measurement keeps using `scheduler_queue` with its `dimensionType` consumer.

**Usage read** (`src/usage/usage.service.ts:31`)
- `findUsageForCustomer` returns `[]` for a customer without an offering instead of throwing `ConflictException`, so the customer usage endpoint responds with an empty result.
